chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Abī al-Miʿzā, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who causes another man to startle, and he injures him, and his riding animal injures another man. He said: “He is liable for whatever occurred of any harm.

And about a thing that is placed on the road, then an animal passes by and startles with its rider and injures him,” so he said: “Everything harmful in the path of the Muslims—its owner is liable for whatever it causes.”

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslims, meaning the public community of believers
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for compensation

ai.seo_question: Who is liable if someone places a harmful object on the road and it causes injury?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes liability for harm caused by frightening others or by placing harmful obstacles in the public road. It indicates a legal principle that whoever creates a harmful condition in the way of Muslims is responsible for the injury that results from it.
